title: BofA No Longer in Talks to Arrange IPO of China’s Moonshot AI
source_used: Bloomberg (first two paragraphs) and TradingView/Seeking Alpha summary of it
key_facts: Bank of America is no longer part of the potential roster of banks working on Moonshot AI's IPO, according to people familiar with the matter (Bloomberg, 14 Oct 2026).
BofA had been in discussions for a role as overall coordinator for the IPO in Hong Kong; the talks did not lead to a formal mandate.
Bloomberg says Moonshot, which it calls the Chinese AI darling, faces scrutiny in the US; no details in the text read.
Seeking Alpha summary: Moonshot was founded in 2023 by Yang Zhilin, is backed by Alibaba, Tencent and 5Y Capital, and drew attention in July with the open model Kimi K3.

Follow-up: our 12 Oct 2026 edition carried a Reuters exclusive that Moonshot executives were in talks to settle a shareholder claim before the Hong Kong listing; our 6 Oct 2026 edition carried the confidential filing.
quote_evidence: Bank of America Corp. is no longer part of the potential roster of banks working on Moonshot AI's initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter, as the Chinese artificial intelligence darling faces scrutiny in the US.
BofA had been in discussions for a role as an overall coordinator for the IPO in Hong Kong, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is confidential.
Founded in 2023 by Yang Zhilin, Moonshot is backed by Alibaba , Tencent , and 5Y Capital.
why_it_matters_hint: A large US bank is out of the running for a role in Moonshot's planned Hong Kong listing, with US scrutiny cited.
notes: Bloomberg text is only the first two paragraphs (paywall); the TradingView summary adds company background. Follow-up of 12 Oct 2026 edition item 15 (Moonshot shareholder dispute). Nothing says the listing is cancelled.
